correctness.rationale: At leaf worlds the two modal subformulas reduce to p; at a nonempty edge-world the premise forces all leaf successors p, hence the conclusion. At the root, failure is exactly a proper two-colouring of every hyperedge, including correct handling of the empty edge family. Rank-one and graph odd-cycle characterizations follow. The parity double-cover and Reingold give L containment. Subdividing every input graph edge and adding st produces an odd cycle precisely on connected terminal pairs, with first-order tuple interpretation, proving L hardness. Monotone NAE-3SAT gives 3-uniform NP hardness, hence coNP completeness of validity. Actual checker passed 62 rank-one, 1099 graph, 1042 rank-three instances and 410 marked-reduction cases, with complete original valuation quantification for smaller instances. These computations are corroboration, not the infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The strongest primary comparison, arXiv:2603.12171v1 §5.4, proves unrestricted coNP-completeness by encoding Set Splitting as McKinsey failure; §5.2 explicitly uses cycle parity for non-first-order definability. These earlier contributions are credited. The newly assessed claim is the complete exact fixed-uniformity complexity spectrum, principally an L-completeness theorem for rank two under first-order reductions proved with a graph subdivision/terminal edge interpretation. Neither targeted scientific searching, previously accessible scientific claim descriptions, nor the material inspected stated this rank-two lower reduction or the whole three-rank spectrum. The easy rank-one test, rank-three hardness via standard 3-uniform two-colouring, and known cycle parity are not presented as individually novel. An unindexed equivalent or an uninspected fuller treatment remains possible.
residual_risks: Unindexed equivalent rank-restricted modal complexity results cannot be ruled out by a database search.

value.rationale: For the natural uniform hyperedge-rank parameter of the three-layer incidence construction in the recent finite-frame correspondence theory, the exact complexity rises from a local FO test at rank one, through L-completeness at rank two, to coNP-completeness at rank three. The matching L lower bound is explicit and uses an unusually weak first-order reduction, locating a natural intermediate computational stratum inside the published coNP-hard validity problem. An exact natural-domain structural and complexity classification is valuable independently of a further downstream theorem; the already known odd-cycle non-first-orderness is credited rather than claimed as novelty.
